result.rationale: The diff's groups_controller.rb #members now does `limit = (params[:limit] || 50).to_i` with no upper bound, whereas the prior code capped automatic groups at 200 (`limit = (params[:limit] || 200).to_i` applied only to automatic groups) — the new code actually removes that safeguard and applies any user-supplied limit to all groups on a public, guardian-checked-only endpoint. Unbounded query+serialization load from a single request is a concrete defect (resource exhaustion) introduced by this change; a cap is a one-line fix.

judged_text: limit = (params[:limit] || 50).to_i has no maximum, so a single request can demand the group's entire membership in one response. Any signed-in user who can see a large group (trust-level automatic groups can have hundreds of thousands of members) sends ?limit=99999999 and forces the server to load and serialize every member row at once — trivially repeatable DB and serialization load on a public endpoint; a one-line cap closes it.

adjudication.rationale: In `GroupsController#members`, the diff introduces `limit = (params[:limit] || 50).to_i` and then uses it directly in `group.users.order(:username_lower).limit(limit).offset(offset)` with no upper bound. This is a public-ish endpoint (guarded only by `guardian.ensure_can_see!`) and the response serializes `members`, so an attacker can request an extremely large `?limit=` value to force large DB reads and serialization work. The finding’s suggested cap is directly applicable to the new code.
